title: PERSISTENCE SPHERES: BI-CONTINUOUS REPRESENTATIONS OF PERSISTENCE DIAGRAMS.
one_liner: Map persistence diagrams into an ordinary linear feature space while preserving both stability to small data changes and enough structure to reconstruct the original diagram continuously.
lead: Topological data analysis summarizes shape by building persistence diagrams: multisets of birth-death points that record when connected components, loops, or higher-dimensional structures appear and disappear across a filtration. Those diagrams are useful but awkward for machine learning because they are sets of variable size equipped with Wasserstein distance rather than ordinary fixed-length features. Existing embeddings, meaning feature maps that turn diagrams into ordinary machine-learning inputs, often lose one of two goals. Some are stable under small perturbations but distort the original diagram heavily. Others keep more detail but lose continuity or invertibility. Persistence spheres aim for both at once. They define a map from diagrams into a linear space that is Lipschitz with respect to 1-Wasserstein distance and also has a continuous inverse on its image. The point is not only accuracy on benchmarks. The point is that the representation changes smoothly when the diagram changes and still retains enough information to recover that diagram continuously.

problem.h2: Why persistence diagrams are hard to use directly in learning systems
paras: A persistence diagram is not a fixed table of values. It is a set of points where each point records when one topological feature appears and when it disappears. Different datasets can produce different numbers of points, so standard learning pipelines cannot consume diagrams directly without a representation change.

That change is delicate. Small perturbations in the data should create only small changes in the representation, because persistence is used precisely for its stability. But the representation should also retain enough detail to distinguish diagrams that are genuinely different. Many existing summaries trade one goal against the other.

callout.html: Build a representation with continuity in both directions, because a good feature map should change smoothly with the diagram and should not throw away essential diagram structure.

steps.text: Take the birth-death point set produced by a filtration on data such as a time series, graph, mesh, or point cloud.
Convert the point set into a function in a linear space, using an explicit formula designed around 1-Wasserstein continuity.

steps.b: Use the function as a learning representation.
steps.text: Run regression, classification, or clustering on the transformed features, because standard linear-space tools can now be applied.
Ensure that small changes in the diagram move the representation only a small amount, so noise does not create abrupt feature jumps.
Keep a continuous inverse on the image, so the representation still determines the original diagram in a stable way.

paras: The paper changes persistence-diagram representation from one-way summarization into a two-way continuous mapping between diagrams and a linear feature space.
object.object: the embedding used to move persistence diagrams into machine-learning feature space

hidden.name: how much of the original diagram structure survives the embedding
paras: The hidden quantity is the fidelity of the diagram after representation: whether the embedded function still determines where the birth-death points were and how they move under perturbation.

This is stronger than ordinary downstream accuracy because a representation can score well on one task while still collapsing many distinct diagrams onto similar features. Persistence spheres target a stricter property: nearby diagrams stay nearby, and distinct diagrams remain separable enough that the inverse map varies continuously on the embedded image.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark the properties that keep the embedded function faithful to the original diagram.

reads.html: The representation should still contain the diagram itself, not only a task-specific summary.
Bi-continuity means the forward map is stable under 1-Wasserstein perturbations and the inverse on the image is continuous, so the embedding preserves diagram structure in both directions.

paras: Forward continuity matters first because persistence diagrams are used in noisy settings. If a tiny perturbation in the input data caused a large jump in the feature representation, the topological summary would become unreliable for learning. The Lipschitz property prevents that by bounding how much the feature representation can move under 1-Wasserstein changes in the diagram.

The inverse continuity matters next because stability alone is not enough. A representation can be very smooth while still merging many different diagrams into almost the same feature. By requiring a continuous inverse on the image, the paper ensures that the embedded object keeps enough structure to recover the original diagram without discontinuous decoding.

The linear-space target matters because many learning methods assume addition, averaging, and ordinary norm-based optimization are available. Persistence spheres move diagrams into that setting without discarding the Wasserstein-based structure that made the diagrams informative in the first place.

math.words: The forward map should move at most proportionally to 1-Wasserstein changes in the diagram, and the inverse on the image should also vary continuously so the original point set remains recoverable.

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose one persistence point moves slightly because the input point cloud was perturbed by a small amount.
The 1-Wasserstein distance between the old and new diagrams is then small.
The Lipschitz property guarantees that the persistence-sphere features also move only a small amount.
If two embedded representations converge toward each other inside the image of the map, the inverse continuity says their decoded diagrams also converge.
Together these two statements give smooth behavior in both directions.

math.note: The central claim is not only a forward bound. It is the pair of continuity properties taken together.

charts.title: One-way persistence embeddings
charts.note: These representations are often usable for prediction, but they may discard too much diagram structure for stable inversion.

charts.title: Persistence spheres
charts.note: The method is strong across tasks because the representation stays stable while retaining enough structure to distinguish diagrams faithfully.

items.b: Setting choice can trade smoothness against resolution.
items.html: If the persistence-sphere settings are too coarse, the representation may blur nearby points together. If they are too fine, numerical estimation can become less stable.

items.b: The inverse matters only on the image.
items.html: Continuous recovery is guaranteed for representations that actually come from valid diagrams, so arbitrary feature-space perturbations may not decode into valid diagrams in a stable way.

items.b: Downstream success can hide representational loss.
items.html: A method can perform well on one benchmark while still discarding diagram information that would matter on another task.

The representation is most convincing when it changes smoothly under 1-Wasserstein perturbations, preserves enough point-set detail for continuous recovery, and remains usable by ordinary linear-space learning methods.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small topological benchmark from noisy circles, figure-eight shapes, and random point clouds. Compute persistence diagrams, transform them with persistence spheres, and compare them against one or two standard persistence embeddings. The demo should test whether small perturbations in the point clouds produce small feature changes, whether nearby embedded features decode to nearby diagrams, and whether the transformed features support classification without losing shape distinctions.
demo.closing: The demo is convincing only if the embedding stays smooth under noise while still retaining enough structure to reconstruct the diagram continuously.
